bull.b: Toast is adding locations while expanding recurring monetization: record Q2 adds lifted the base to about 180,000, while ARR and recurring gross profit grew 25% and 28%. A larger installed base supports durable subscription and payments growth through product adoption and transaction volume.

Toast has moved from losses to meaningful GAAP profitability, with Q2 operating income at a 26% margin and adjusted EBITDA at a 37% margin. This inflection, alongside raised 2026 guidance, indicates operating leverage can compound as the platform scales.

Effectively zero debt, solid equity and improved returns give Toast flexibility to fund product expansion without heavy financing constraints. Minimal leverage also reduces refinancing exposure and allows more operating cash to support growth initiatives and absorb business volatility.

bear.b: Hardware and professional-services gross profit was negative and created an 11% drag on recurring gross profit in the quarter. Memory-driven hardware cost pressure could persist into 2027, potentially limiting consolidated margin expansion despite software progress.

TTM revenue reached $6.80B, but growth slowed to about 5.6% from much higher rates in 2021–2023. This deceleration raises the need for continued location additions, product attach and new-market execution to sustain Toast’s next phase of expansion.

Operating expenses rose about 19% as Toast funds core expansion, new markets and AI, with sales and marketing and R&D growing rapidly. Although strategic, this investment can defer margin gains and make near-term profitability more dependent on execution.
